sara: heads up — saw a p95 latency regression on INT8 AWQ after yesterday's packing change. seems specific to short seqs with KV cache hits.

bench-bot: detected regression in /perf/runner: p95 went from 6.1ms -> 8.9ms for seq<=16, batch=1, kv-hit=true (model: x-l7-int8-awq, kernel=packed-int8).

liam: thanks for flagging. is this only AWQ-weighted models or GPTQ too?

bench-bot: quick summary:
```
seq=8 batch=1 kv_hit=true
AWQ+packed-int8: 8.9 ms/token
AWQ+no-pack : 5.4 ms/token
GPTQ+packed-int8: 6.2 ms/token
GPTQ+no-pack: 5.8 ms/token
fp16-packed: 7.0 ms/token
```

vikram: interesting — packing adds overhead for cache hits because we avoid cross-request batching so we pay pack/unpack per request. for short sequences the kernel startup dominates.

maria: also saw calibration differences: AWQ group_size=128 gave slightly worse accuracy but smaller quantized footprint; group_size=32 had better quality but packing cost increased because more metadata?

sara: here's a short repro command I ran: `./perf_runner --model x-l7-awq --kernel packed-int8 --seq 8 --batch 1 --kv_cache=true --iters 2000`

liam: initial thought: our kernel selection heuristic prefers packed kernels for int8 broadly because they win on throughput, but we don't account for kv_cache hits or per-request seq length distribution. we should make chooser aware of `kv_hit` and `observed_seq_percentiles`.

vikram: agreed. propose heuristic tweak: if kv_cache_hit_rate>0.6 and p50_seq_len<32 and batch_size==1 then prefer `no-pack` int8 kernel. also add a microbenchmark to compute per-model break-even latency for packing.

maria: calibration note: when we force group_size lower for AWQ (g=32) we get smaller MSE but the quantized GEMM becomes less friendly to vecized kernels, so packing performance swings. tradeoff table attached below (from local calib).

bench-bot: snippet from profiling (nvprof-like):
```
Kernel: int8_packed_pack_unroll   42.1%  (pack costs)
Kernel: int8_matmul_kv_hit        30.3%
Kernel: cuda_memcpy_async         12.0%
Other                          15.6%
Total per-token: 8.9 ms
```

sara: real user impact: short-chat flows (autocomplete + context hits) see worse p95. long seqs unaffected. so we should hotfix chooser before routing more traffic to this model.

liam: minimal change plan: 1) add rule in kernel chooser for kv-hit short requests 2) ship as config flag `runtime.int8.avoid_packing_on_kv_hits` for canary 3) run perf canary in prod subset.

ops-bot: flag created: `runtime.int8.avoid_packing_on_kv_hits` default=false. set to true on canary cluster: canary-3.

vikram: one more nuance — AWQ's group_size interacts with packing microkernel tiling. with g=128 packing aggregates contiguous weight slabs making SIMD friendly, but increases per-request pack cost for small seqs. g=32 reduces pack contiguity so matmul kernels have less throughput. we need to include `group_size` into the break-even estimator.

maria: suggestion: extend profiler to export a small per-model table: for seq in [8,16,32,64] measure packed vs unpacked single-request latency and pick kernel per-seq bucket at runtime. cheap to store and check when `kv_hit=true`.

sara: that sounds good — simple mapping: `if kv_hit: use seq_bucket_lookup(seq_len)` and the lookup picks `packed` or `nopack` based on measured p50. avoids complex heuristics and is data-driven.

liam: can we do an even cheaper on-the-fly estimator? e.g., a sync call to `perf_cache.get(model, seq_bucket)` which falls back to measured defaults. avoid blocking code path.

bench-bot: implemented microbench harness: `perf_cache` entries for x-l7-awq -> {seq8: no-pack, seq16: no-pack, seq32: packed, seq64: packed}. numbers saved estimate p95 -25% on canary.

ops-bot: canary rollout scheduled: canary-3 -> 5% traffic on 2026-03-18T12:40Z with flag enabled. monitor p95, error rate, token throughput.

vikram: also plan to add packing latency breakdown to runtime traces (per-request pack/unpack times) so we can correlate with kv_hit flags.

maria: QA: we need to re-run eval prompt sets to ensure AWQ g=32 calibration doesn't regress NLL by >0.5% compared to baseline. I'll run eval after canary warms.

sara: actionable checklist:
- liam: patch chooser + perf_cache read path (PR)
- vikram: add pack/unpack trace spans (PR)
- maria: evals for AWQ g=32 vs g=128 (job)
- ops-bot: enable flag on canary and roll metrics (ops)

liam: I'll open PR in ~1h, will include pseudocode and perf harness.

sara: thanks everyone. if canary shows improvements we'll flip flag global and add per-model defaults to the model catalog. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: monitoring alerts: p95 for x-l7-awq on canary currently: 5.6ms (down from 8.9ms), error rate stable.

maria: noted — starting eval runs now, will post results in this thread.

liam: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4287 (kernel-chooser: kv-aware seq-buckets)

sara: merging once CI green. follow-ups in #eng-ml if needed.
